entries.question: Addison casts [Ferocious Zheng]. After it resolves, they cast [Elemental Eruption] and reveal [Everdream] from their hand, splicing it onto Elemental Eruption. Storm reads "When you cast this spell, copy it for each other spell that was cast before it this turn," and copying a spell copies both its characteristics and all decisions made for it, including targets and modes [702.40a] [707.10]. Since the spliced Everdream text is part of Elemental Eruption's characteristics on the stack, each copy has it too. Note also that text gained by splice which refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack — so on each copy, any "Everdream" text acts as Elemental Eruption [702.47c] [201.5b]. Targets for the added text are chosen normally when casting, and you may choose new targets for any of the copies [702.47d] [702.40a].

One caveat: the splice text only lasts while that spell is on the stack — Elemental Eruption loses the splice changes once it leaves the stack for any reason [702.47e]. That doesn't affect the copies, which are separate spells on the stack that already have the text.

entries.question: Albert and Nico are beginning the game and have just drawn 7 cards. Albert has [Serum Powder] in their hand. Does Albert get to know whether Nico is going to mulligan before deciding whether to use Serum Powder's ability?
entries.reason: The candidate says it depends on turn order and could allow Albert to know Nico's choice if Nico is the starting player, whereas the reference states Albert does not know Nico's decision (Albert being the starting player), so the final rulings conflict.
entries.answer:
It depends on turn order, not on Serum Powder itself. Albert may use Serum Powder's ability at the moment Albert would declare whether to take a mulligan [103.5b]. Mulligan declarations are made in turn order: the starting player declares first, then each other player in turn order [103.5b]. So:

- If Albert is the starting player, Albert must decide about Serum Powder (and about mulliganing) before Nico has declared anything — Albert does not know Nico's choice.
- If Nico is the starting player, Nico declares first, so Albert does know Nico's declaration before using Serum Powder. Note that a declaration is only whether Nico will mulligan; all mulligans are actually taken simultaneously afterward, so Albert won't see Nico's new hand [103.5b].

Also, rule 103.5b explicitly says the "any time you could mulligan" action need not be taken in the first round of mulligans, and that other players may have already made their mulligan declarations by the time the player has the option to perform it. After performing the action, Albert then declares whether to take a mulligan [103.5b].

Multiplayer: with more than two players the same principle applies — everyone after the starting player knows the earlier declarations in turn order [103.5b]. Additionally, in a multiplayer game (and Brawl) a player's first mulligan doesn't count toward cards put on the bottom of the library or the number of mulligans allowed [103.5c][800.6]. In a shared-team-turns game, the starting team declares first, in any order among themselves, and teammates may consult [103.5d][805.3a].

The provided context doesn't include Serum Powder's card text, so this answer covers only the timing/information question, assuming Serum Powder's ability is usable "any time you could mulligan."

entries.question: Ariana controls [Sen Triplets], which targeted Nico. Nico's hand contains [Rift Sower]. Can either player suspend it? If so, who will cast it once the last time counter is removed?
entries.reason: The candidate allows Nico to suspend the card (unless something prevents him), but the reference states neither player can suspend it, so the final rulings conflict.
entries.answer:
Direct answer: only Nico could possibly suspend Rift Sower, never Ariana — and if Sen Triplets stops Nico from casting spells, then neither player can. If Nico does suspend it, Nico is the one who may cast it when the last time counter is removed.

Why:

1) Suspending is a special action, not a cast. Rule 116.2f: "A player who has a card with suspend in their hand may exile that card," and they may do so only if they could begin to cast that card by putting it onto the stack [116.2f, 702.62a]. The card must be in *that player's* hand. Rift Sower is in Nico's hand, not Ariana's, so Ariana cannot take the suspend special action on it even though Sen Triplets lets her play cards from Nico's hand — Sen Triplets grants permission to play, and suspending is expressly not playing/casting the card [702.62a].

2) Nico's ability to suspend depends on whether anything prohibits him from casting. Rule 702.62c: when determining if you could begin to cast a card with suspend, take into account any effects that would prohibit that card from being cast; rule 601.3: a player can begin to cast a spell only if no rule or effect prohibits it. So if Sen Triplets' effect prohibits Nico from casting spells, Nico cannot satisfy the "could begin to cast" condition and cannot exile Rift Sower with suspend either. Caveat: Sen Triplets' and Rift Sower's actual card text were not provided to me, so I can't confirm from the given materials that Sen Triplets contains a casting prohibition; I'm giving you the rules test to apply to whatever its printed text says. A card's own text overrides general rules where they conflict.

3) Who casts it later. The third suspend ability reads "When the last time counter is removed from this card, if it's exiled, you may play it without paying its mana cost if able" [702.62a]. The "you" is the player who exiled it with suspend — Nico. Nico would be the caster and controller of the resulting spell [112.2a]. Ariana does not get to cast it off Sen Triplets, because at that point Rift Sower is in exile, not in Nico's hand. If it's a creature spell cast this way it gains haste [702.62a]. Casting it that way uses the alternative-cost rules [702.62d].

Multiplayer note: nothing here changes with more than two players. Sen Triplets targets one opponent, and only that opponent (the owner of the hand) can take the suspend special action; other players' hands are unaffected.
